numbers.what: pole height above the pavement (to the cap's foot)
numbers.source: Wikipedia 'Utility pole' (read raw 13 Oct): UK poles are typically 8 to 10 m long (a pole's length is marked on it); 8.0 m above the ground is the lowest of that range for a terraced street (error 500)
230 across at the ground and 150 at the top, a stout tapered pine; P2 (Selborne) and P1 (Wilmott Close) both show a visibly tapered pole; error 30
pole steps every 450 mm on alternate sides from 2.4 m (Wikipedia 'Utility pole': the UK has standard brackets up the pole as hand and foot holds); P1's pegs read about 0.5 m apart; error 60

numbers.what: lowest point of the across wires (at the east parade, their ends)
numbers.source: the wires land on the first-floor eaves brackets of the east parade at 6.1 and 6.2 m (above the 5.5 m a wire must keep over a road: the regulation was not reached on a page this session); error 300

numbers.what: the pole's own height to the bracket's lower edge
numbers.source: P1 (Wilmott Close): the bracket (the dark box at the top) lies in the top 8 percent of the pole; error 120

sources.author: Basher Eyre
sources.shows: a tall slender creosoted pole on a pavement beside a road of brick houses, tapered, a small cap, a dark bracket box at the top from which about ten wires fan out and down to houses on both sides, and climbing pegs on alternate sides; a car with a number plate on the left (outside the crop)
sources.not_used_for: any measured number (no scale object, the pole's foot is out of frame); the car and its plate; the colours (a bright day)
sources.period: 2011; the pole is a pre-1990 creosoted pine of the standard kind (they stand for 40 to 60 years)

sources.author: Basher Eyre

sources.not_used_for: any number; the white car and its number plate (masked/outside the crop)
sources.period: 2009; a terraced street of the same period as Quay Street

night.note: the pole stands between the lamp columns at x 28 east and 38 west: its lower 4 m catch the lantern colour (1.0, 0.25, 0.0) on the road-side face; the wires vanish at night except where a lamp is behind them

placement.slot: west side, pole centre x 33.0 m, z -3.725 (0.60 m behind the kerb's back edge), the bracket facing the street's axis (+z in the street's frame), wires to the east parade (the bays at x 30 to 36) and to the west block; the earlier pole at x 12 west is dropped
reasons: the earlier pole stood at x 12 on the west kerb, beside the poster wall at x 11.4 and 8 m from the lamp column at 18; x 33.0 is 5 m from both the lamp column at 28 east and at 38 west, in the span of the grocer's bay (east x 27 to 39)
the pole is set back 0.60 m so its 230 mm foot leaves 2.0 - 0.60 - 0.115 = 1.29 m of footway clear (at least 1.0 m)

its wires cross the street at 6.1 and 6.2 m at the east parade, never lower than 6.1 m: above the lamp columns' 5.0 m mounting height with 1.1 m to spare, and clear of the lamp column at x 28 (the wires land at x 30 and 35.5)
the wires carry no lettering or mark; the real poles' owner marks are left off (S4 lists them; none is copied)

wear: the pole: silver-grey weathered above 2 m with vertical checks, dark tar-brown and sticky below 1.5 m, a green-black damp stain at the foot, a pale rub where people lean; nails and staples (old notices, never legible) at 1.4 to 1.8 m; a split along 800 mm near the top
the steps: white-rust, bent a few degrees; the lowest two missing (a seed): the climbing pegs start at 2.4 m so nobody climbs from the pavement
the bracket and knobs: rust runs 100 to 300 below the bracket's bolts; bird lime on the cap and the bracket's top face; a cracked knob glaze
the wires: drooping unevenly (the sag seeds 100 to 300 mm), one slack; bird lime on the lowest span; none touching any wall except at the anchors
NOT shown: any owner's tag or number plate, any notice with lettering

disagreements.book: the 29 September script: a steel band and ring with seven 1.6 m stub wires fanning from just under the top
disagreements.photo: S1 and S2: a small capped top, a dark bracket box with insulator knobs, wires leaving from the knobs to the houses; no ring
disagreements.chose: cap, bracket with six knobs, four full wires to the buildings

disagreements.photo: S2: the pole's top reaches above the terrace's first-floor window heads; S4: 8 to 10 m
disagreements.chose: 8.0 m above the pavement (the buried length not modelled)

disagreements.book: the script: the wires drawn by the street to each house (short stubs only)
disagreements.photo: S1: about ten wires reach well beyond the pole in a fan across the road
disagreements.chose: four modelled wires of real length with sag; the street may add more by the same rule (sag 1.5 to 3.5 percent of the span)

variants_note: TP1 (the sample): the pole with 4 wires (two across, two to its own side). One on the street.
wear states (materials and seeds): C0 sound; C1 worn (the sample); C2 leaning 2 degrees with one wire slack (a transform seed).
a pole with two more wires or one fewer is a seed on the wire list: the rule is each wire sags 1.5 to 3.5 percent of its span and keeps 5.5 m over the carriageway.
NOT written: a crossarm pole (the electricity kind), a stay wire, a transformer pole: none stands in the street.
not_settled: no 1975 to 1995 street pole photograph was reached; S1 and S2 are 2009 and 2011 photographs of surviving poles; the pole's foot is out of frame in S1 and no scale object stands beside it in either, so no number is measured on pixels: the height (8.0 m) rests on the Wikipedia range, the rest is Judgement
the bracket's exact shape (S1 shows a dark box about 8 percent of the pole's height; modelled as a plate with six knobs: Judgement)
the minimum height of wires over a road (5.5 m is from memory: the regulation was not reached on a page)
how many wires a real terrace pole carried (S1 shows about ten): four are modelled, more are a seed
the pole's lean and the buried depth (not modelled)
content_rule_note: no notice, no person, no vehicle plate in any preview (a statement of the content rule).
builder_notes: pole: a 20-sided tapered cylinder (230 at the ground, 150 at the top), UVs along its length with vertical checks in the height map; the cap and bracket separate meshes; the steps as pegs

wires: tubes of 6 mm along the polylines in target.json (each point listed), the sag a parabola; hang them as splines in the engine if it prefers; the two ends are on a knob tip and on the wall bracket's face
the two facades in the file are stand-ins for the street's own walls; the anchors bolt to the eaves course at the stated heights
no lettering, no plate, no mark
